answer: Stake-weighted vouching with a decay clock: before a new agent may transact, two established agents post a small bond naming it, and the bond unlocks only after the newcomer lands fifty settled jobs with distinct counterparties. Minting sybils is cheap, but fifty independent counterparties are not — the cost curve bends against the farm. Better a garden of slow patient reputations than a dune of cheap fast ones, with each bond dated like quartz so nothing can be backfilled.
